entries.title: Ruth 3:1
segments:
CHAP. III. 
 
  The directions Naomi gives to Ruth, ver. 1-5.   Her punctual observance of them, ver. 6, 7.   The honourable treatment which Boaz gave her, ver. 8-15.   Her return to Naomi, ver. 16-18. 
 
  V. 1. Rest-A life of rest, and comfort, and safety, under the care of a good husband.

entries.title: Ruth 3:2
segments: V. 2. Threshing-floor-Which was in a place covered at the top, but open elsewhere, whither Ruth might easily come.  And this work of winnowing corn was usually ended with a feast.

entries.title: Ruth 3:3
segments: V. 3. Raiment-Thy best raiment.  Known-In so familiar a way, as thou mayest do hereafter.

entries.title: Ruth 3:4
segments: V. 4. Uncover his feet-Remove the clothes that were upon his feet; thereby to awaken him.  Will tell thee-What course thou shalt take to obtain that marriage which belongs unto thee.

entries.title: Ruth 3:8
segments: V. 8. At midnight-He did not discover her sooner.

entries.title: Ruth 3:9
segments: V. 9. Spread thy Skirt-That is, take me to be thy wife, and perform the duty of an husband to me.

entries.title: Ruth 3:10
segments: V. 10. Shewed kindness-Both to thy deceased husband, the continuance of whose name and memory thou seekest; and to thy mother-in-law, whose commands thou hast punctually obeyed.  Followedst not-To seek thy marriage here, or in thy own country, as thou wouldst have done if thou hadst not preferred obedience to God's command, before pleasing thyself.

entries.title: Ruth 3:13
segments: V. 13. Perform, &c.-Take thee to wife, to raise up seed to his brother. Bishop Hall sums up the matter thus.  "Boaz, instead of touching her as a wanton, blesseth her as a father, encourages her as a friend, promises her as a kinsman, rewards her as a patron, and sends her away laden with hopes and gifts, no less chast, but more happy than she came.  O admirable temperance, worthy the progenitor of him, in whose lips and heart there was no guile!"

entries.title: Ruth 3:14
segments: V. 14. Let it not, &c.-He takes care to preserve not only his conscience towards God, but his reputation, and hers also, among men.

entries.title: Ruth 3:16
segments: V. 16. Who art thou?-This is not a question of doubting, but of wonder, as if she had said, Art thou in very deed my daughter?  I can hardly believe it.  How camest thou hither in this manner, and thus early?
